english.title: Possess prohibited ammunition - military equipment
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without the authority of the Secretary of State, had in your possession **(..SPECIFY ITEM OR OBJECT..), which was designed to be projected as a missile from a weapon and which was designed to be or had been incorporated in ammunition

(A)_[for military use consisting in or incorporating a missile designed to explode on or immediately before impact]_
(B)_[for military use consisting in or incorporating a missile designed so that a substance contained in the missile would ignite on or immediately before impact]_
(C)_[for military use consisting in or incorporating a missile designed so, on account of its having a jacket and hard-core, to penetrate armour plating, armour screening or body armour]_
(D)_[designed to be used with a pistol and incorporating a missile designed or adapted to expand on impact]_
(E)_[containing or designed or adapted to contain any noxious liquid, gas or other thing]_
(F)_[which was designed or adapted to expand on impact]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(1A)(g) of, and Schedule 6 to, the Firearms Act 1968.

english.notes:
(i) Section 5(7)(a) of the Firearms Act 1968 provides that a rocket or ammunition is to be taken to be for military use if it is designed to be capable of being used with a military weapon.
(ii) Section 5(7)(b) provides that a missile designed so that a substance contained in it will ignite on or immediately before impact includes a missile containing a substance that ignites on exposure to air.
(iii) Section 5(7)(c) provides that a missile expanding on impact includes a missile deforming in any predictable manner on or immediately after impact.
(iv) Section 5A of the Act contains exemptions.
(v) A rocket or ammunition is considered to be for military use if it is capable of being used with a military weapon.
(vi) See also offence wordings: H2797 and H2798.
(vii) On conviction for this offence, the court can order the forfeiture or disposal of any firearm or ammunition and cancellation of any firearm certificate or shot gun certificate, and any firearm or ammunition subject of such order may be seized or detained by a constable (section 52 of the Firearms Act 1968).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

For offences committed on or after 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.
